Primer01

LCARS is the computer interface of Starfleet in the Next Generation era: black screens, colored bars bent into elbows, and labels in tall, condensed capitals. This site explains how it is built, era by era, and gives you the tokens to build it yourself.

The name

LCARS stands for Library Computer Access/Retrieval System. Michael Okuda designed it for Star Trek: The Next Generation in 1987, and it carried on through Deep Space Nine, Voyager, the four TNG films and the series since. The crew nicknamed the screens Okudagrams, after him.

Film, not screens

Most panels on set were not screens at all. They were sheets of black film with shapes cut out of them, colored by hand with gels and lit from behind by fluorescent tubes under a diffusion sheet. That is where the look comes from: a pure black ground, flat opaque shapes, and no gradients, glows or shadows. The black never changed; the colors could.

Okuda’s rules

Gene Roddenberry asked for a ship that was extremely user-friendly. Asked what that meant for LCARS, the Okudas answered:

“I interpreted this to mean that there should be extremely clear organization of very complicated information.”

Michael and Denise Okuda, TrekToday Q&A, 1999

So every panel groups something. A frame holds one subject, and its sidebar indexes it.

“I was not particularly concerned with matching colors closely because of the notion that the panel could reconfigure itself based on the software.”

Michael Okuda, quoted by Wrath of Dhan

He said it of the bridge backlits, which were remade as they wore out and never matched exactly. This system reads it as a license: geometry and black are fixed, and the hues belong to the era.

Roddenberry also asked, as Wikipedia puts it, that the panels not have a great deal of activity on them. So motion is a garnish: a blink is a hard step, never a fade.

47

Codes and 47

The small print on LCARS is codes, not prose: section numbers, readings, crew initials. Many are in-jokes, and the number 47 most of all: writer Joe Menosky started it, and the staff and art department spread it across the franchise. This site numbers its sections the way the screens do, and its sidebar code, DS-09, counts the rows it heads.

What this system is

A design system distilled from those screens, in three layers:

  • Tokens. Every color role for every era and mode, and the type, in the Design Tokens Community Group format, plus dist/tokens.json, the same values resolved to plain hex.
  • Specs. Anatomy, type, the pill and the guidelines, written without reference to any medium.
  • Implementations. Terminal pills in impl/shell, the CSS behind this page, and an Obsidian theme in LCARS Mainframe.

Canon comes first. Every color is what the screen shows, measured from frames or reconstructed from them. None is adjusted to meet a contrast target. Where a value is a stand-in, its theme says so.

Anatomy02

LCARS has a small grammar. Learn these pieces and you can read a panel from any era. This page is built from them: the elbow at the top left, the title cut into the top bar, the sidebar of blocks, and a heading cut into a bar at every section.

The pieces

Unit, uOne point of the reference layout. Every length is a whole multiple of it, so a panel scales as one piece.
Gap3u of black between every pair of shapes. There is one gap, and it never varies. Meter segments, 1u apart, are the only exception.
BarA thick solid shape: 36u for a frame’s top bar (its arm), 22u for a section heading, 20u for a row.
ElbowThe corner that joins the top bar to the sidebar. One painted piece with two radii: an outer sweep equal to the arm, and an inner fillet a third of it. Never a sharp inner corner.
SidebarThe elbow’s leg, 112.8u wide (about 3.1 arms), carried on below the elbow as a stack of blocks a gap apart.
OverrunHow far the arm runs past the leg, and the leg below the arm: 0.6 of the arm.
CutWhere a title interrupts a bar. The text’s cap height equals the bar, a gap of black sits on each side, and the bar runs on.
StubA short segment in a counter color, breaking up a long bar.
End capA run that stops ends in a separate half-round cap, a gap away. An end that meets an elbow or another bar stays square.
BlockA sidebar block or button. Its label sits bottom right, in dark ink.
FieldThe black area the frame encloses. Content lives here, never on the frame.

Color on shape

Dark ink on color; color on black. Text on a bar or block is set in the page’s own black, and text on the page is colored. Never white text on a bar. The frame itself carries no text: titles cut into it instead.

Canon proportions

Screen panels pair a thin arm with a wide sidebar. This system defaults to the reference layout, with a thick arm and a small fillet, which holds up at small sizes. The canon ranges below come from edge-fitting six elbows in three Memory Alpha captures (Descent, Part II, Yesterday’s Enterprise and Equinox, Part II).

MeasureThis systemTNG capturesVOY captures
Sidebar ÷ arm3.17.1 to 7.63.8 to 4.6
Inner radiusarm ÷ 30.8 to 2.2 × arm, median 1.3
Outer radius1 × arm1.9 to 5.1 × arm
End capshalf roundflatter, 0.73 to 0.85 of a half roundtrue half round

The full geometry, with the rules for building an elbow in code, is in spec/anatomy.md.

Lower Decks · 2020–2024

Mike McMahan calls Lower Decks “our version” of the TNG era, just hand drawn: butter, honey and harvest gold on black, with orange stubs and an October-sunset alert. The colors are thelcars.com’s Lower Decks set; which color plays which role is this system’s reading.

Source: Fan reconstruction (thelcars.com Lower Decks colors, https://www.thelcars.com/colors.php: butter, daybreak, harvest gold, honey, october sunset, orange, pumpkin pie). thelcars publishes the colors by name, not by role; the role assignment is ours, after the TNG theme's structure. No production hex values exist for Lower Decks.

Color04

Components never name a color. They name a role, and the theme fills it in. Structural roles say how LCARS is built; semantic roles say what a reading means. The tables follow the page’s mode.

No green

No LCARS era uses green for success, so ok is a blue in every theme. Green would read as a different design language. Red appears only for alerts, and an alert always comes with words.

Escalation

Like a ship going from normal operations to red alert, escalate in steps, and only as far as the situation needs. Identity colors (accent to accent-5) say what a pill is; status colors say how it is.

1 · NormalShields100%Lit, value in value or ok.
2 · ApproachingShields38%The value turns warning, or the block does.
3 · CriticalShields9%The value or the block turns alert.
4 · Act nowShieldsdownThe pill blinks. Keep blinking pills rare; two at once compete.

The reverse holds too: a reading with nothing to say goes off rather than disappearing, when its absence would itself confuse.

Modes05

A mode cuts across themes. Every theme resolves every role in every mode, so anything written against roles works in any combination.

DarkThe screen: the default, and the only canon mode.
LightA pale page with dark text, for reading in daylight. Headings, alert text and data take the era’s dark colors mixed toward black in OKLab (45%, 40% and 45%), unless the era measured its own.
PrintInk on paper. Printing this page switches it to print mode on its own.

Type06

LCARS reads through its type: tall, condensed capitals, packed tight.

Two faces

Okuda has said he mostly used Helvetica Ultra Compressed, and Letraset Compacta besides. Bitstream’s digital cut of the Helvetica is Swiss 911 Ultra Compressed. Both are commercial, so this system sets display text in Antonio, an open-licensed condensed face, and running text in Lato. Never set display text in a regular-width face; LCARS reads through its condensed caps.

USS Enterprise NCC-1701-D

Cap height equals the bar

When display text sits in a bar, the bar sets the size: font-size = bar ÷ 0.859375, Antonio’s cap height. Trim the line box to the cap height above and the baseline below, with text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic, and the caps fill the bar exactly: cap tops meet its top edge, the baseline sits on its bottom edge. A 36px bar takes 41.89px type.

TrimmedOK
UntrimmedNO

The dashed box is the text’s line box. Untrimmed, it carries the font’s ascent and descent, and the caps float off the bar’s edges.

Levels

LevelSampleWeightTrackingFit
titleEnterprise NCC-1701-D700-0.06embar
row-labelMain engineering400-0.05embar
headingSensor analysis400-0.05embar
labelDeflector array400-0.04emfree
bodyRunning text reads as written, in Lato.4000emfree
metaSD 41153.7 · 47-B400-0.025emfree

bar levels take their size from the bar they sit in; free levels use the medium’s reading size. Negative tracking also lands after the last letter, which narrows the black after a title, so pad the end by the tracking to even it out.

Pill07

The pill is this system’s own component, built from LCARS parts: one labeled reading, for status lines, readouts and navigation. Pills sit in a row and wrap as whole units.

Start capHalf circle, radius 0.5h, block color.
Label blockBlock color, label in label-ink, uppercase, 0.5h padding after the label.
ValueOn the page, in the value color, 0.5h gap each side.
End capHalf circle, radius 0.5h, block color, standing alone.

States

LitvalueOffvalueBlinkvalue

Off is an unlit button: present, readable and quiet. Blink alternates lit and dimmed every 1s, where dimmed is each channel × 0.4, snapped to the 0x33 grid. With reduced motion it holds lit and marks the end cap with a dashed outline.

In use

A system readout:

CTX42%5H8%7D91% ↻TueDisk▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░ 120G freeModelOpusBRmainDiffclean

A navigation row with an alert indicator:

Path~/code/lcarsBRfeaturePR#12 APPRDiff+12 -3Err1

Terminals draw the caps with the Nerd Font half-circle glyphs U+E0B6 and U+E0B4; see impl/shell.

Use it08

From JavaScript

Pin a release straight from GitHub; the package is not on npm.

"devDependencies": {
  "lcars-design-system": "github:JawsomeJason/lcars-design-system#semver:^0.7.0"
}
const tokens = require('lcars-design-system'); // dist/tokens.json
const { theme, mode } = tokens.default;        // 'tng', 'dark'
const roles = tokens.themes[theme].modes[mode];
roles.ok;                                       // '#8899ff'
tokens.type.capRatio;                           // 0.859375

Every theme lists every role as plain hex in each mode. TNG in dark mode, in part:

tokens.themes.tng.modes.dark = {
    "frame": "#ea9c72",
    "block": "#baa4e5",
    "accent": "#8899ff",
    "ok": "#8899ff",
    "warning": "#eb943a",
    "alert": "#ff2200"
  }

The DTCG source is exported too (lcars-design-system/tokens/*), but read the resolved file: it has no aliases to follow.

From CSS

This page runs on two stylesheets you can copy: roles.css, generated, sets --lcars-<role> for any element with data-theme and data-mode; lcars.css draws frames, elbows, cut headings, blocks and pills from them. Both ship in the package under docs/.

<html data-theme="voy" data-mode="dark">
  <div class="frame"><div class="elbow"></div>…</div>

From a shell

LCARS_DS=${LCARS_DS:-$HOME/code/lcars-design-system}
. "$LCARS_DS/impl/shell/palette.sh"
. "$LCARS_DS/impl/shell/pill.sh"
lcars_pill accent PATH "$PWD" && printf '%s\n' "$lcars_pill_out"

Set LCARS_THEME to choose an era.

Versions

Releases are git tags with GitHub releases, listed in the changelog. A major version removes or renames a role, theme or mode; a minor adds one, adds a spec, or changes a color; a patch changes words only. Below 1.0 a breaking change bumps the minor instead, so pin with a caret.

Built with it

  • LCARS Mainframe: an installable Obsidian vault with an LCARS theme in every era.
  • impl/shell: pills for truecolor terminals and zsh prompts.
